concept.name: Breakaway gap
concept.definition: A gap that occurs as price breaks out of a trading range or congestion area, interpreted as marking the start of a new directional move. Breakaway gaps are conventionally expected NOT to be filled soon, distinguishing them from common gaps; the classification remains an interpretive heuristic.
concept.intuition: The market escapes its cage in one jump — enthusiasm is so strong that price skips the boundary levels entirely.
concept.mechanics: Identified by location (at the boundary of a congestion area or chart pattern) and by volume, which should pick up significantly. The breakout point is then expected to act as new support (upside break) or resistance (downside break); a prompt fill argues against the breakaway reading.
concept.failure_modes: A gap out of a range that is quickly filled was a false breakout with extra steps; low-volume breakaway gaps are especially suspect.
concept.misconceptions: That a breakaway gap will soon be filled, offering a better entry; the whole point of the classification is that waiting for the fill often means missing the move.
concept.example: ChartSchool's example: after weeks of consolidation and a low-volume poke above resistance, a stock gaps up on high volume, starting a new uptrend — a breakaway gap.

citations.source: StockCharts ChartSchool — Gaps and Gap Analysis
